mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate signals a robust demand environment that boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when the federal funds rate is above 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 5% signals a tight labor market that drives wage growth and inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when the unemployment rate is below 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts and a decrease in the unemployment rate signal a strong demand environment that boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when housing starts are increasing and the unemployment rate is decreasing (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production signals a decrease in supply chain activity that reduces corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when industrial production is declining (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 3% and a decrease in the consumer price index signal a monetary tightening cycle that reduces inflation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the federal funds rate is above 3% and the consumer price index is decreasing (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment signals a strong labor market that drives wage growth and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when payroll employment is increasing (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales and an increase in the unemployment rate signal a weak demand environment that reduces consumer spending and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when retail sales are decreasing and the unemployment rate is increasing (t-test p > 0.05).
